_about: Teaching catalog for the StampLC configuration surface. One source of truth, rendered by four surfaces: the Logic Studio Network panel, the on-device /setup page, the plc> console 'explain'/'learn' commands, and AI tools. The firmware table (src/config_explain_table.inc) is GENERATED from this file by scripts/generate_config_explain.py; the public Studio reads a copy exported to web/public/config-catalog.json. Writing rule (the lab's ethos): 'firmware' states what the code DOES (observed); 'why'/'security' state what it MEANS (inferred).

_schema.key: stable id (matches the UI field + netcfg verb)
_schema.firmware: what the code does with it (file/function/register)

ip_address.label: IP address
ip_address.plain: A number that names one device on a network, like a street address. Written as four parts, e.g. 10.13.37.10.
ip_address.why: Two devices on the same network must have different addresses; a clash means neither is reachable.
ip_address.explore: Run `netcfg json` - the 'link' field is the address the hardware is actually using right now, which can differ from what you configured until the next reboot.

subnet_mask.label: Subnet mask
subnet_mask.plain: Decides which addresses count as 'my local network' versus 'somewhere else I reach through the gateway'. 255.255.255.0 means the first three parts must match to be local.
subnet_mask.why: Too narrow and the device thinks neighbours are remote (sending everything to the gateway); too wide and it never uses the gateway at all.
subnet_mask.firmware: Passed to the W5500 (eth_begin) or the WiFi stack (setup_wifi WiFi.config) as the netmask; the IP stack ANDs it with each destination to pick local-vs-routed.

gateway.label: Gateway (router)
gateway.plain: The address the device sends traffic to when the destination is NOT on its own local network - the door to everywhere else.
gateway.why: Wrong gateway = the device talks to its local neighbours fine but can't reach the internet, an NTP server, or an MQTT broker on another network.
gateway.firmware: Stored as eth_gw / wifi_gw and loaded at bring-up. Note: in DHCP mode the firmware ADOPTS the gateway the DHCP server hands out.
gateway.security: Because the gateway is also the default NTP source, a rogue DHCP server that names itself the gateway becomes the device's time source - the AiTM path explored in the NTP lab (Part 8).

dhcp_vs_static.label: DHCP vs. Static
dhcp_vs_static.plain: DHCP = the network hands the device an address automatically. Static = you pin a fixed address yourself.
dhcp_vs_static.why: DHCP is easy and avoids clashes; Static is predictable (you always know where the PLC is) and is what plant networks use so controllers never move.
dhcp_vs_static.firmware: use_static flips eth_begin/setup_wifi between Ethernet.begin(mac, ip, ...) (static) and a DHCP lease request; on DHCP the firmware also adopts the leased gateway/DNS.
dhcp_vs_static.security: DHCP trusts whatever answers first. A rogue DHCP server can hand out its own address as gateway+DNS+NTP (option 42) and sit in the middle. Static addressing removes that attack surface - one reason ICS networks pin PLC addresses.

sta_vs_ap.label: WiFi STA vs. AP
sta_vs_ap.plain: STA (station) = the device JOINS a WiFi network you already have. AP (access point) = the device HOSTS its own little network that you connect to.
sta_vs_ap.why: You use AP to set the device up when it has no network yet (connect your phone to it, open its web page). You use STA for normal operation on your real network.
sta_vs_ap.firmware: wifi_mode selects WiFi.mode(WIFI_STA) + WiFi.begin(ssid,pass) vs WiFi.mode(WIFI_AP) + WiFi.softAP(ssid,pass) in setup_wifi.
sta_vs_ap.security: An AP that anyone can join, or that keeps a default password, is an open door to the controller - see the setup-AP credential note.

eth_present.label: W5500 Ethernet present
eth_present.plain: Whether the wired-Ethernet add-on (the W5500 PoE module) is physically fitted.
eth_present.why: WiFi is always built in; wired Ethernet only exists if the module is installed, so its settings only matter when it's present.
eth_present.firmware: eth_ok() returns true when Ethernet.hardwareStatus() detects the W5500 chip over SPI at boot; the config UI hides/greys the Ethernet section when it's false.
eth_present.explore: Boot log prints `[ETH] hardware=<n> link=<n>`; hardware=0 means no module (normal on a WiFi-only unit).

eth_mode.label: Ethernet addressing
eth_mode.plain: Whether the wired interface gets its address automatically (DHCP) or uses a fixed one you set (Static).
eth_mode.console: netcfg eth static <ip> <gw> <mask>  |  netcfg eth dhcp
eth_mode.explore: netcfg json -> eth.mode (configured) and eth.link (what the hardware is using now).

eth_ip.label: Ethernet IP address
eth_ip.plain: The fixed address other machines use to reach this device over the wired network.
eth_ip.why: Must be unique on the wired segment and inside its subnet, or Ethernet clients can't connect.
eth_ip.firmware: eth_ip -> the W5500 source-IP register via eth_begin() before any socket opens.

eth_gw.label: Ethernet gateway
eth_gw.plain: The router address the wired interface uses to reach other networks.
eth_gw.firmware: eth_gw; also the default NTP source when no NTP server is set.

eth_mask.label: Ethernet subnet mask
eth_mask.plain: Which wired addresses count as local vs. routed through the gateway.

wifi_mode.label: WiFi mode
wifi_mode.plain: Off = no WiFi radio (contained). STA = join your network. AP = host a setup network.
wifi_mode.why: Default is Off so a lab device never joins a network by surprise. Use AP to provision, STA to run.
wifi_mode.firmware: wifi_mode drives setup_wifi(): WIFI_OFF / WIFI_STA+begin / WIFI_AP+softAP.
wifi_mode.security: Leaving WiFi Off is the contained default - enabling a radio widens the attack surface, so do it only on an isolated segment.

ssid.label: WiFi network name (SSID)
ssid.plain: The name of the WiFi network you want the device to JOIN (station mode).
ssid.why: Must match an existing network exactly (case-sensitive) or the device can't connect.

pass.label: WiFi password
pass.plain: The password for the WiFi network you're joining.
pass.firmware: pass -> WiFi.begin(ssid, pass). Stored in NVS; the config JSON never returns it.
pass.security: Treated as a secret: the device's /api/config and netcfg json never echo it back.

wifi_addr.label: WiFi addressing
wifi_addr.plain: Whether the WiFi interface gets its address automatically (DHCP, usual on a home/office LAN) or fixed (Static).
wifi_addr.firmware: wifi_use_static; setup_wifi() calls WiFi.config(ip,gw,mask) only when static.
wifi_addr.console: netcfg wifi static <ip> <gw> <mask>  |  netcfg wifi dhcp

wifi_ip.label: WiFi IP address
wifi_ip.plain: A fixed address for the device on your WiFi network (static mode only).

wifi_gw.label: WiFi gateway
wifi_gw.plain: The router on your WiFi network (static mode only).

wifi_mask.label: WiFi subnet mask
wifi_mask.plain: Which WiFi addresses are local vs. routed (static mode only).

ap_ssid.label: Setup-AP name
ap_ssid.plain: The name of the temporary WiFi network the device hosts in AP mode so you can set it up.
ap_ssid.why: You connect your phone/laptop to this, then open the device's web page to configure it.
ap_ssid.firmware: ap_ssid, or a default built from the chip's MAC (setup_ap_ssid -> esp_read_mac) so two boards don't collide; WiFi.softAP(ssid,pass).
ap_ssid.explore: In AP mode the device serves its config page at http://192.168.4.1:8080/setup.

ap_pass.label: Setup-AP password
ap_pass.plain: The password for the device's own setup network.
ap_pass.security: The DEFAULT password is a deliberate teaching weakness (CWE-798/1392, hard-coded/default credentials): a device left on its default AP password is trivially joined. Change it, or use AP only briefly to provision then switch to STA/Off.
ap_pass.firmware: ap_pass or the documented default (setup_ap_pass); WiFi.softAP(ssid, pass) - WPA2, min 8 chars.

ntp.label: NTP time source
ntp.plain: The server the device asks for the current time. Blank means 'use the gateway'.
ntp.why: A correct clock matters for logs and certificates; a wrong one can push the device past the Year-2038 rollover.
ntp.security: If time comes from the gateway and the gateway came from DHCP, whoever controls DHCP controls the clock - the NTP AiTM / Y2038 lab (Part 8).

cfg_cred.label: Remote-config credentials
cfg_cred.plain: The username and password that protect the device's web/API configuration.
cfg_cred.security: Ships as admin/openplc - a default credential (CWE-798/1392). Anyone who can reach the web page can reconfigure the device until you change it.
cfg_cred.firmware: cfg_user/cfg_pass checked by the web server's basic-auth on /api/config.
